result.rationale: The diff shows the merge branch still uses `booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"))` to locate the old calendar event for deletion, while the same function was refactored to process `calendarReference` as an array via `filter`. Since this PR makes bookings carry multiple calendar references (collective hosts' destination calendars creating events per destination), `find` only selects the first old reference, so other hosts' old calendar events would not be deleted, leaving orphaned events.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, `calendarReference` was changed from a single reference (`find`) to an array (`filter`) and the update loop now processes all `_calendar` references. However, the merge cleanup path still uses `const oldCalendarEvent = booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"));` (inside `if (newBookingId)`), which will only delete one old calendar reference/event. With the new multi-destination/multi-reference behavior, this leaves other `_calendar` references (e.g., collective hosts) undeleted/orphaned.
